A.lede: The minimum fee is what you're actually paying.

rows.label: A $500 minimum
rows.sub: of your media spend, before a single ad is made

rows.label: A $1,000 minimum
rows.sub: the percentage never comes into it at all

B1.lede: Three models. One charges you for your own growth.

rows.label: Typical range
rows.sub: of monthly media, most common at higher budgets

rows.label: The failure mode
rows.sub: double the budget and the invoice doubles, for work that didn't

rows.label: Typical range for SMEs
rows.sub: a month and beyond, depending on scope

rows.label: The failure mode
rows.sub: stable until scope and spend come apart

B4.lede: Base fee plus a share of results.

rows.label: The share
rows.sub: of verified revenue, profit or leads above a baseline

rows.label: The failure mode
rows.sub: it all rests on how that is set, and who verifies it

B5.lede: Ask what this fee does at double my spend.

C.lede: A competitor's ad is evidence of a decision, not a result.

D.kicker: Working out what you actually pay
D.lede: The fee you're quoted isn't the fee you pay.

rows.label: Add up
rows.sub: management fee, creative cost, platform and reporting fees

rows.label: Then divide by media spend
rows.sub: almost always higher than the headline number

D1.lede: The fee you're quoted isn't the fee you pay.

D2.lede: Add everything that leaves your account.

rows.label: The management fee
rows.sub: the number on the proposal

rows.label: Creative production
rows.sub: quoted separately in most arrangements

D3.lede: Divide the total by your media spend.

rows.label: What you get
rows.sub: the only number worth comparing between providers

rows.label: Why it matters
rows.sub: a fee excluding creative is paying for half of it

D4.lede: What happens at double my spend, and what do I own at the end.

E.lede: Sort by how long an ad has been live, not by how many there are.

F.lede: Automation amplifies whatever it is given.

F1.lede: It automates the part that used to be the job.

F2.lede: All of this, at no extra cost.

rows.label: Handled by the platform
rows.sub: audience discovery, placement, budget distribution, iteration speed

rows.label: What that was
rows.sub: a large share of what a percentage was justified by

F3.lede: The part that actually decides the account.

rows.label: Still entirely yours
rows.sub: it cannot make your ads, only choose between them

rows.label: And
rows.sub: broken tracking, what a customer is worth, when a winner went stale

F4.lede: It raised the floor and moved the constraint. It didn't remove it.

G.lede: Most testing concludes nothing because it tests the wrong thing.

rows.label: What usually gets tested
rows.sub: same idea, new headline, new background, new button

rows.label: What actually moves it
rows.sub: a different reason to care, a different opening three seconds

G1.lede: Test angles against each other, not variants.

G2.lede: Ship new concepts weekly, not in one monthly batch.

G3.lede: Let a test leave the learning phase before you conclude anything.

G4.lede: Judge on cost per result. Click-through rate flatters bad ads.

G5.lede: Document the losers. The pattern in them is the real output.

H.lede: When frequency climbs, the creative is the problem.

I.lede: Theirs has to be renewed. Yours has to be earned.
